newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sees Romania-Hungary pact as step towards EU.
newsitem.headline: France sees Romania-Hungary pact as step towards EU.

text.p: France hailed a treaty signed on Monday to end centuries-long disputes between Romania and Hungary as a decisive step towards their entry into the European Union.

President Jacques Chirac cabled congratulations to the leaders of the two countries over the pact which recognises inviolability of borders and guarantees the rights of Romania's 1.6 million ethnic Hungarians, the foreign ministry said.
It said Paris had spared no effort to encourage the treaty which is in line with the Pact of Stability in Europe signed in Paris three years ago.
"France stresses the decisive importance of this step, including regarding the enlargement of the European Union," the ministry said.

Chirac, on a visit to Warsaw last week, said France would welcome Poland's membership of the EU by the turn of the century. The EU Commission later said membership could only be realistically envisaged by 2002.
